sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 of the 1909 Newark volume five, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows a narrow strip of the Newark and Irvington boundary country along Clinton Avenue, which runs down the left of the page, with Alpine Avenue on the right. The sheet is turned about 74 degrees, so the streets that cross Clinton Avenue run across the page: Montgomery Avenue and 21st Street at the top and South 20th, 19th and 18th Streets below. Above the Town of Irvington line, in block 3018 A, lies a large vacant tract with a few frame dwellings and outbuildings at its upper left. Below it, in blocks 3018 and 3017, narrow lots on South 20th and South 19th Streets carry small frame dwellings, mostly two storeys, with a plumbing shop and a drug store at the foot of the sheet near Fabyan Place. Several streets are drawn with water pipe lines and a hydrant. Alpine Avenue is marked Not Opened on the upper right. A boundary line is lettered Town of Irvington and City Line across the vacant area. The compass rose on the lower left shows north toward the upper right, and a scale of feet is at the bottom. Adjoining sheets 42, 44 and 55 are named at the edges.
notes: Alpine Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap today.
Placed from three junctions along Clinton Avenue, all on one line: low confidence in rotation.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 of the 1909 Newark volume five, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 74 degrees, shows the Newark and Irvington boundary district between Alpine Avenue on the left and Madison Avenue on the right. Montgomery Avenue and 21st Street run in parallel diagonal bands across the upper half of the sheet, with the Town of Irvington City line lettered across the middle. The lower half is divided by South 20th, South 19th and South 18th Streets, which run across the page. The upper blocks hold J. Rosinger's pickle works with its steam and electric light plant, some frame dwellings and large unbuilt lots, and a row of dwellings on Montgomery Avenue near Madison Avenue. In the middle, block 3015 holds Wm. Lukes' manufacturer of special hardware, with a watchman, steam and lights, beside rows of two-storey frame dwellings, with a lumber yard in block 3014 at the lower right. The left blocks are largely empty, with two dwellings at the bottom. Alpine Avenue is marked Not Opened on the upper left. Water mains are shown in the streets with hydrants. A compass rose at the right shows north to the upper right. Adjoining sheets named at the edges are 42, 43, 45, 46, 55 and 72.
notes: Alpine Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap today.
Fitted by helmert through three points all on Madison Avenue (two detected, one hand-picked at the lower edge): low confidence.

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 of the 1909 Newark volume five, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows the Irvington end of Springfield Avenue where it meets South Grove Street, Harrison Place and 22nd Street. Springfield Avenue crosses the upper left of the page as a wide band running to the northeast, lettered 85 feet in width, with Harrison Place and 22nd Street leaving it to the south. At the left South Grove Street, with North Grove Street opposite it at the edge, has a row of two-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots in block 3. Between Harrison Place and 22nd Street, in block 2, a long row of frame dwellings, many marked 2 1/2 storeys, stands on the 22nd Street side, with lots to the Harrison Place side mostly vacant. On the Springfield Avenue side, dwellings stand along numbers 771 to 801, and a fire alarm box stands at the corner. To the right of 22nd Street, in block 1, dwellings with a few stables and a cooperage face Madison Avenue. The bottom is cut by Alpine Avenue. A compass rose at the top shows north to the upper left. Adjoining sheets named at the edges are 30, 42, 44, 46 and 47.
notes: Placed from one junction (Springfield Avenue and Harrison Place) with scale 7.58 px/ft and rotation from its lines: low confidence.
South Grove is modern Grove Street; North Grove Street is not in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 of the 1909 Newark volume five, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows the Irvington side of Springfield Avenue where it runs between Avon Avenue, 21st Street, Madison Avenue and Montgomery Avenue. Springfield Avenue crosses the upper left as a wide band running to the northeast, with 21st, 22nd and 23rd Streets running north of it. South of it 22nd Street and 21st Street run down the page as parallel diagonal bands to Madison Avenue at the bottom, and Montgomery Avenue runs from the lower centre to the upper right with S. 20th Street beside it at the right edge. The blocks between hold rows of two- and three-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a few stables and a cement works, a steel engraver's shop (J. Carl) and a paint shop. Avon Avenue crosses the upper right. The Town of Irvington and City line is lettered down the right centre as a broken line, and the blocks there are numbered 2640 and 2641, with 1, 2 and 3 on the south. A fire alarm box and hydrants are shown. A compass rose at the lower right shows north to the upper left, and a scale of feet is at the foot. Adjoining sheets named at the edges are 44, 45, 47, 72 and 73.
notes: Names were read from the overview at reduced size, not on 1:1 crops (medium confidence).
23rd Street is not in OpenStreetMap today.

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 of the 1909 Newark volume five, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the south-western part of the Irvington district around Springfield Avenue and the Essex County Speedway. The sheet is turned: its streets lie at an angle to the page, with a north arrow at the lower left. The top strip shows the end of the built blocks along Madison, Brookside, Avon and Woodlawn, with frame dwellings and a few outbuildings on narrow lots between Myrtle Avenue and Brookside Avenue. Below it the Essex County Speedway and its East Speedway Avenue cross the sheet from left to right, and the large middle of the sheet is left blank apart from a single small building beside N. Grove. On the right the blocks of Berkeley, Brighton and Argyle terraces are laid out in long rows of narrow lots, ending at the N. Grove roadway, and continue on sheet 48. The lower half is a wedge of ground on both sides of Springfield Avenue, with 22nd and 23rd streets, a short 20th Avenue, Standard Place and 21st Street, carrying dwellings, small shops and a noodle works. The bottom edge carries the Princeton library stamp and the 50 foot scale note, and the sheet touches sheets 45 and 46 on the left and below, 28 and 30 above, and 48 and 5 to the right.
notes: Placed only from lot corners shared with sheet 48 (anchored, low confidence); the street junctions of this sheet did not detect.
The Berkeley, Brighton and Argyle terrace streets of the 1909 sheet appear in OpenStreetMap as Berkeley Terrace, Brighton Terrace and Argyle Terrace but run much longer today.
Garden State Parkway and other later roads cross this sheet's modern line positions; the drawn Springfield Avenue wedge does not match them.
100 ft, turned. Mostly blank Essex County Speedway; placed from one lot corner carried from 48 (low).

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 of the 1909 Newark volume five, at 100 feet to an inch, shows a block of Irvington lying between Argyle Terrace on the west and Tichenor Terrace on the east, from Myrtle Avenue at the top to 21st Street and the Newark city line at the bottom. The sheet is turned, with the north arrow at the upper left. The upper strip carries Delmar Place, Tremont Terrace and 19th Avenue between Myrtle Avenue and West Speedway Avenue, with scattered dwellings. The Essex County Speedway and East Speedway Avenue cross the sheet from left to right. Below them seven narrow terrace streets run down to N. Grove: Argyle, Tremont, 19th Avenue, Highland, Bernard, Breakenridge and Tichenor, laid out in long rows of narrow lots, mostly empty, with the Irvington Varnish and Insulator Company works beside Tremont Terrace (shown in detail in an inset on sheet 21), a mill beside N. Grove and a few dwellings. South of N. Grove the blocks between 23rd, 22nd and 21st streets and 19th and 18th avenues are filled with dwellings and small shops, and at the lower left the Schanz and Koehler bar fixture works stands on Nelson Place. A dotted line labelled Town of Irvington City Line crosses near the bottom edge; South 20th Street lies beyond it. Adjoining sheets are 47 on the left, 49 on the right and 74 to 76 below.
notes: Bernard Terrace has no match in OpenStreetMap; the modern diagonal 18th Avenue lies along its line.
19th Avenue / 21st Street and 19th Avenue / 22nd Street were rejected or excluded because the modern junction is 8 to 11 m from the drawn one.
The Irvington Varnish and Insulator Company works is repeated at 50 feet to an inch as part 2 of sheet 21.
100 ft, turned. Terraces Argyle to Tichenor, Speedway, Irvington Varnish and Insulator Co.; 19th Av south of Grove left out.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 of the 1909 Newark volume five, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the Irvington and Vailsburg district between Tichenor Terrace on the left and 15th Avenue on the right, from Munn Avenue at the top to 21st Street and South 20th Street at the bottom. The sheet is turned, with the north arrow at the upper right. At the top, Munn Avenue and Linden Avenue run across the sheet beside long blocks of narrow, mostly vacant lots numbered in the 4000 series, with Grove Terrace between them and a rounded block at the left. Myrtle Avenue crosses obliquely below Linden, and the Essex County Speedway with its West and East Speedway avenues forms a wide band through the middle. Below the speedway the blocks of Tichenor, Montrose, Grove and Arverne terraces carry rows of small dwellings, while on the right Speedway Avenue, Oak Avenue and Vine Avenue cross the blocks between 16th Avenue, Roosevelt Place and 15th Avenue. The Grove Street Public School, in pink, stands south of N. Grove at the left, and the lower blocks between 22nd, 21st and South 20th streets are largely empty lots. The Town of Irvington city line runs along the bottom. Sheets 48 and 50 lie to the left and right, and 77 and 78 below.
notes: The 21st Street and South 20th Street junctions were left out of the fit: they lie 8 to 13 m from their modern positions.
16th Avenue / Grove Street is excluded as displaced by about 6 m.
Roosevelt Place is Roosevelt Terrace in OpenStreetMap; Grove Terrace at the top is West Grove Terrace.
100 ft, turned. Tichenor to 15th Av, Munn / Linden; 21st St and South 20th St left out (8-13 m).

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 of the 1909 Newark volume five, at 100 feet to an inch, shows the Vailsburg end of the Irvington district between 15th Avenue and South Orange Avenue. The sheet is turned, with the north arrow at the upper left. The top is occupied by South Munn Avenue and the Vailsburg Bicycle Track, an oval with a grand stand, bleachers and a quarter-mile and old third-mile track. Below it lies Electric Park, an amusement ground with a merry go round, scenic railway, theatre, dance pavilion and Japanese village, with a short Devine street along its lower edge. The left half of the sheet is cut by Rodwell Avenue, Speedway Avenue, Oak Avenue and Vine Avenue between 15th and 14th avenues, with small dwellings on narrow lots and some larger buildings such as the Vulker knife works near N. Grove. Dassing Avenue, West Side Avenue, Whitney Street and Grove carry a denser frontage of frame dwellings and a few shops towards South Orange Avenue on the right, with long blocks numbered 4001 to 4013. The Town of Irvington city line and South 20th Street lie along the bottom. Sheet 49 adjoins on the left, 79 and 80 are below, and the ends of South Munn and North Munn avenues are lettered at the top.
notes: Only seven junctions were detected; the N. Grove junctions did not detect and the placement leans on the Oak, Whitney and Speedway streets.
Drawn West Side Avenue corresponds to Gladstone Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
100 ft, turned. Electric Park, Vailsburg bicycle track, North Grove; 7 points (low-medium).
